questions.stem: Why is ammonia converted to urea in the liver rather than being excreted directly?

options.text: Because ammonia is too large to pass through the kidney's filtration barrier
Because ammonia is not soluble in water
Because the kidneys can only filter urea, not ammonia
Because ammonia is highly toxic and urea is much less harmful

questions.explanation: Ammonia is extremely toxic even in small amounts. The liver converts it into urea, which is much less toxic and can be safely transported in the blood to the kidneys for excretion.
